newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics seen as locomotive for rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics seen as locomotive for rally.

text.p: Taiwan electronics shares, especially semiconductor stocks, surged again at mid-morning on Tuesday, with investors accepting the trendsetting sector as a reliable locomotive for the market's new rally, brokers said.
With 80 minutes left, at 0240 GMT, electronics had surged 3.66 percent, while the overall index was up 1.34 percent.

Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor was up the daily seven percent limit to T$109, its second limit-up in as many days. Rival semiconductor maker United Microelectronics had gained T$3 or 3.41 percent to T$91.
"Electronics are widely seen as a locomotive leading the overall index to new highs, probably over 9,000 points in the coming months," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
"Since electronics have the best outlook among Taiwan's industries, investors now can accept a higher price-earnings ratio for the sector," Hung said.

In the past, the market had seen high-tech stocks as rather risky and tolerated P/E ratios at around 20, below the broader market average. That perception has changed as the sector has matured, and investors now accept P/E ratios of 30.
"Investors now see the sector's P/E ratio at some 30, which equals to the overall market's average," he said.
Hung forecast United Microelectronics' earnings per share at T$2.76 in 1997 and T$4.14 in 1998. A P/E ratio of 30 would point to a reasonable market price of T$82.8 to T$124.2.
He forecast Taiwan Semiconductor's earnings per share at T$3.9 in 1997 and T$5.5 in 1998, which would translate into a market price of T$117 to T$165 at a P/E of 30.

"Investors buying electronics are foreseeing the sector's sound 1998 outlook, so we can use their 1998 earnings per share as the indicators to judge their prices," he said. "Therefore, despite that their share prices have surged in recent months, most semiconductor shares still have room to rise further."
